messages.content: Thanks—I appreciate the encouragement. The test ran this morning, and the double cloth held moisture about twice as long. Not perfect, but a solid improvement. I’m leaning into the sand idea for the next round. Fingers crossed for round two.

That’s great news—a double the retention is a significant improvement! Let me know what happens next time you move the plants into those larger pots with the sand. I'm looking forward to hearing how the next iteration of the test goes!

Yeah, every little boost helps, especially with how spotty the power is here. I’ve started pre-moistening the sand with cooled boiled water—cuts down on algae without chemicals. Going to monitor the root temp over the next few days; if it stays stable, we might actually have something. I’ll send notes once the data settles.

That sounds like a smart approach—controlling the environment with the sand should definitely help with those algae issues! Please keep me updated on how the root temperature monitors look; I'm keen to hear if those results settle into a solid pattern!

For sure—I’m tracking it in a notebook for now, nothing fancy. The roots seem happier already, less mushy. If this keeps up, I might try splitting one of the plants next week to test propagation in the sand mix. Worst case, I lose a cutting and learn something. Either way, progress. I’ll shout either way how it goes.

result.content: That sounds like a very practical, hands-on approach—learning through experimentation is exactly how things move forward. Please let me know when you've got a sense of the final results from splitting the plant next week; I'm curious to see what the next test round shows!
